author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell described the surreal experience of being adored and revered by Hollywood one moment, only to watch nearly forty percent of everything he earned get carved up between agents, managers and lawyers the next. He said you eventually realize you're just a temporary placeholder doing a job, not the star the industry makes you feel like. He argued the classic movie star, the Leonardo DiCaprio or Timothée Chalamet type, barely exists anymore, replaced by influencer culture where figures like Andrew Tate get maligned in ways that a Burt Reynolds type would have simply been celebrated for in an earlier era. Is Hollywood's magic really gone, or was it always this sinister underneath?

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacted to Britain's plan to ban social media for anyone under 16, pushing back hard on the claim that it's being done to protect children. He argued that if child protection were truly the priority, the country would look completely different, from vaccine safety to school diets to a welfare state that actually shows up before a crisis hits. He said you can't let a generation grow up with nothing but their phone and then use their wellbeing as the excuse to tie every citizen's internet use to verifiable ID. Was this ever really about protecting kids, or was it about something else entirely?
